record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Let K be a plane tree in R^2 with diameter 1 and let epsilon be positive. A tree is epsilon-chainable if it is the union of closed sets C_1,...,C_n, each of diameter less than epsilon, such that C_i intersects only its immediate neighbors C_{i-1} and C_{i+1}. A tree is epsilon-spanned if two non-intersecting round disks of diameter epsilon with centers moving on K cannot move so that their traces on K are the same. Is every epsilon-spanned plane tree of diameter 1 necessarily 10 epsilon-chainable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a plane tree (a compact, connected, locally connected, one-dimensional planar continuum without simple closed curves) of diameter $1$, and let $\varepsilon>0$.

Say that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-chainable if there exist closed sets $C_1,\dots,C_n$ with $K=\bigcup_{i=1}^n C_i$, each $C_i$ of diameter strictly less than $\varepsilon$, such that $C_i\cap C_j\neq\emptyset$ if and only if $|i-j|\le 1$.

Say that $K$ is $\varepsilon$-spanned if there do not exist two continuous motions of two disjoint round closed disks of diameter $\varepsilon$, whose centers move along $K$, such that the two centers trace out the same subset of $K$ during the motion.

Decide whether the following is true: every $\varepsilon$-spanned plane tree $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of diameter $1$ is necessarily $10\varepsilon$-chainable.
